_meta.name: English
_meta.note: HD Doc interface strings. Keys are read by core.tr(); a missing key falls back to en.json. To add a language: copy this file, translate the values, set _meta.name to the language's own name, and save as lang/<code>.json (the file name is the language code) - no code change needed. The _meta block itself is documentation only and is never shown in the UI.

gui.title: HD Doc v{ver}
gui.about.title: About
gui.about.body: HD Doc - a read-only, HD Tune style disk error scanner.
gui.hint: Tip: smaller segments = live map (~1s each); whole-disk is fastest but maps at the end; quick reads head samples only
gui.perm_standard: Permission: standard user (admin required for physical disks)
gui.map_title_health: Disk health heatmap (fixed {n} cells · green=OK · red=read error)
gui.map_title_speed: Disk read speed heatmap (fixed {n} cells · color = read latency)
gui.log.admin_ok: Running with administrator rights; physical disks can be scanned
gui.log.not_admin: Not running as administrator. Scanning physical disks (\\.\PhysicalDriveN) requires administrator rights, otherwise fio cannot open the device and every block reports "failed to open file".
gui.log.not_admin_linux: Not running as root. Scanning physical disks (/dev/sda, /dev/nvme0n1, ...) requires root, otherwise fio cannot open the device and every block reports "failed to open file". Launching from the app icon pops up the pkexec prompt automatically; if it does not appear, click "Restart as root", or run from a terminal: sudo python3 HD_Doc.py.
gui.log.elevate_handover: Authorization granted / elevated instance starting; this process exits...
gui.log.no_pythonw: pythonw.exe not found; a console window may appear after elevation
gui.log.bs_clamped: Block size exceeds disk capacity; adjusted to {sz}
gui.log.quick_plan: Quick scan: {n} regions, {sample} sampled each (total {total}, {pct:.2f}% of capacity)
gui.log.quick_region_enlarged: Quick scan: segments of {set} would create too many regions (one fio launch each); regions automatically enlarged to {actual}
gui.log.quick_no_size: Quick scan needs a known capacity to place samples evenly; capacity unknown, falling back to a single full pass
gui.log.no_size_map: Could not query target capacity; the heatmap shows whole-disk aggregate stats only (no positional detail); fio will still auto-detect the device size and complete the scan
gui.log.stop_requested: Stop requested. Note: fio's per-block latency log is written only on normal exit; after a forced kill the current segment's heatmap data is lost (progress/error counts are kept up to the last second before the stop)
gui.log.no_engine_probe: Cannot probe the fio engine list; skipping engine check
gui.log.readonly_note: Read-only scan of {t}; nothing will be written to the disk
gui.log.fio_missing: fio executable not found: {f}. Windows: winget install fio.fio
gui.log.no_size_degraded: Cannot query the capacity of {t}; falling back to whole-disk-at-once: no live progress/speed/ETA, the heatmap appears only after the scan, and stopping midway loses per-block data
gui.msg.no_target: Please select or enter a scan target first
gui.msg.admin_needed: Scanning {t} requires administrator rights (fio must be elevated to open \\.\PhysicalDriveN). Click "Restart as administrator", or restart without --no-elevate.
gui.msg.admin_needed_linux: Scanning {t} requires root (fio must open the block device as root). Click "Restart as root" (pkexec graphical authorization), or run from a terminal: sudo python3 HD_Doc.py
gui.msg.elevate_failed:
Cannot restart as administrator: {err}

Right-click this program and choose "Run as administrator".
gui.msg.already_root: Already running as root; no elevation needed.
gui.msg.elevate_waiting:
Waiting for authorization (pkexec prompt)...
On success the app reopens as root; cancel to keep current rights.
gui.msg.elevate_cancelled:
Elevation did not complete (pkexec exit code {code}): authorization cancelled or denied by polkit.
If no prompt appeared, run from a terminal: sudo python3 HD_Doc.py
gui.msg.elevate_no_display:
No graphical display detected (neither DISPLAY nor Wayland); automatic elevation skipped.
A root instance could not connect to the display. For GUI elevation, run inside a desktop session, or from a terminal: sudo python3 HD_Doc.py
gui.msg.elevate_timeout:
Authorization wait timed out ({secs}s): the prompt has been closed.
Retry "Restart as root", or run from a terminal: sudo python3 HD_Doc.py
gui.msg.engine_bad:
Current fio does not support the '{e}' engine; scan not started.

Engines actually supported by this fio:
{list}

Note: libaio / posixaio are native Linux engines; the Windows build of fio does not include them and fails with "failed to load engine". On Windows use {win}.
gui.msg.exit_scanning: A scan is in progress. Exit anyway?
gui.banner.clean: Scan complete: {ok}/{n} blocks OK, {slow} slow, {err} read errors.
gui.banner.errors: Scan found {n} error blocks (fio error segments {es}). The disk may have physical damage; back up important data immediately. See the Error blocks tab.
gui.banner.stopped_with_errors: Scan stopped by user. {n} error blocks were found before the stop (fio error segments {es}); see the Error blocks tab.

gui.sum.state_stopped: Scan state   : stopped by user (uncovered areas are not errors)
gui.sum.read_errors: Read errors  : {n} blocks (fio error segments {es}, unlocated error lines {ul})
gui.sum.uncovered: Uncovered    : {sz} (a segment failed early; scan incomplete!)
gui.sum.unread_tail: Unread tail  : {sz} (less than one block; fio skips it; not an error)
gui.sum.aborted_note: Note: the scan was aborted; results below are incomplete.
